slice: Red-team the rendered Werkle formation room for genuine human legibility and scanability after a too-shallow mechanical font-size repair.
sharedContext: Ben approves the dark-purple direction and believes copper/orange fits it.
The prior pass raised several labels from 12.48px to 14px and explanatory small copy to 15px, but Ben reports that it barely corrected the real legibility problem.
The page is dense: hero, arrival explanation, formation readout, actor switch, twelve decision topics, shared floor, retained history, and local-device save disclosure.
Formation mechanics and member answers are protected. This is a visual reading/hierarchy review, not a state-model redesign.
The reviewer must judge the actual human scan path, not merely WCAG-like numeric thresholds.
liveStrings: A match opened the door. It did not create a partnership.
Agreement is a state, not a vibe.
No score means compatible. These states only show what the two people have actually decided.
Your latest Intake · self-reported, not verified
Only mutual decisions enter this room.
This practice draft is not saved to your Werkles account and will not follow you to another browser or device.
knownGaps: Compact labels now satisfy a 14px floor but may remain visually subordinate or tiring.
Warm paper cards sit inside dark-purple section containers, creating several competing contrast systems.
Source/provenance lines are important but repeated and visually dense.
The mobile route contains twelve substantial cards and could become an exhausting wall even without horizontal overflow.
No fresh actual cousin has reviewed the post-legibility rendered page.

ENDER.vision: Make the formation room readable at a glance and humane over a long decision session without flattening the approved dark-purple character.
ENDER.pull: Review hierarchy, contrast, type scale, spacing, density, repeated provenance, interaction cues, narrow-width scan path, and cognitive fatigue.
go: Return GO, PATCH, or REJECT and rank the first five legibility failures by human harm.
Give exact visual remedies, not generic requests for more contrast.
Separate information that must remain visible from information that can move behind progressive disclosure without harming trust.
Define one coherent desktop hierarchy and one mobile hierarchy for the first decision card.
ENDER.momentum: Name the smallest patch that would make Ben immediately feel this was more than a token font-size correction.
ENDER.outOfLane: No implementation, new task, subagent, schema, provider call, push, deploy, secrets, spend, or formation-state redesign.

BEAN.vision: Make sure a legibility cleanup does not hide who said what, whether wording is mutual, or the synthetic/local-only boundary.
BEAN.pull: Attack any progressive-disclosure or visual simplification proposal for trust laundering.
go: Return only P0/P1 trust findings that affect the visual patch.
Name which provenance and consent signals must remain continuously visible.
Reject visual noise that looks like legal safety but does not help a member understand the current state.
BEAN.momentum: Supply one plain-language trust hierarchy for a single topic card.
BEAN.outOfLane: No broad product redesign, implementation, provider work, schema, push, deploy, secrets, or spend.
